deep.reconstruction:
OVERALL. Every symbol on the page contains the index 6. Each 3-index symbol ij6 is paired with the 4-index symbol formed by the complement of {i,j} in {1,...,6}. Examples: 146 goes with 2356; 126 goes with 3456 (written 4536); 456 goes with 1236. I write P_ij := (ij6)·({1..6}\{i,j}) for i,j in {1,...,5}. The context (bundle AbelTheta, characteristic-style labels, the line 45+15+25+35=0) strongly suggests these are theta quantities (theta-constants or their squares) attached to genus-2 half-period characteristics. α, β, γ would then be Rosenhain-type moduli or branch-point parameters written as theta quotients. This reading is my interpretation; the page itself does not define the symbols.

(1) Definitions.
- α = 146·2356/(156·2346) = P14/P15
- β = 246·1356/(256·1346) = P24/P25
- γ = 346·1256/(356·1246) = P34/P35

(2) Factorisations stated.
- α−β = P12·P45/(P15·P25). On the page: 126·456·1236·4536 over 156·256·2346·1346.
- αβ−1 = P13·P23/(P15·P25). On the page: 136·236·2456·1456 over the same denominator.
- α−γ = P13·P45/(P15·P35). Here '4526' = 2456 is the complement of 13, so it is correct.
- β−γ = P23·P45/(P25·P35).
- By the evident pattern (my addition): αγ−1 = P12·P23/(P15·P35) and βγ−1 = P12·P13/(P25·P35).
- The first of these is a three-term (Plücker / Ptolemy) relation P14·P25 − P24·P15 = P12·P45. The second is a genuinely different relation. Together they are theta identities, asserted rather than derived here.

(3) Square roots (pure consequences of (2)).
- √[(α−γ)(β−γ)/(αβ−1)] = P45/P35 = 456·1236/(356·1246).
- √[(β−γ)(αβ−1)/(α−γ)] = P23/P25 = 236·1456/(256·1346).
- √[(αγ−1)(αβ−1)/((α−γ)(α−β))] = P23/P45 = 236·1456/(456·1236).

(4) Four quantities. Riemann lists 1, (βγ−1)/((α−β)(α−γ)), (αγ−1)/((β−α)(β−γ)), (αβ−1)/((γ−α)(γ−β)). Under them he writes 456·1236, 156·2346, 256·1346, 356·1246. So these quantities are proportional (up to sign conventions) to P45², P15², P25², P35².
- By Lagrange interpolation the last three sum to 1 (my addition). This yields a linear relation among the four squares P45², P15², P25², P35².
- That is a quartic theta relation. It matches his note '45+15+25+35=0', a statement that the four characteristics sum to zero (a Göpel-type group of four).

(5) Auxiliary identity.
- He first writes (αγ−1)(αβ−1) − α²(βγ−1) = α² − α(β+γ) + βγ.
- He then corrects with the term (1−α²)(βγ−1), arriving at the correct identity (αγ−1)(αβ−1) − (α²−1)(βγ−1) = (α−β)(α−γ).
- Divided by (α−β)(α−γ): (αγ−1)(αβ−1)/((α−γ)(α−β)) − (α²−1)(βγ−1)/((α−γ)(α−β)) = 1.
- In P-language (my addition): P23² − (P14² − P15²) = P45². That is a further quadratic relation, P14² + P45² = P15² + P23².

(6) Cross-ratio-type quotient. (α−β)/(α−1/β) = β(α−β)/(αβ−1) = P12·P45·P24/(P13·P23·P25). The page writes this as (126·456·1236·4536)/(136·236·2456·1456) times 246·1356/(256·1346), which is correct.

(7) Exploratory bookkeeping.
- He compares 126·1236·246/(136·236·1346) with the same expression with 6 replaced by 5, i.e. 125·1235·245/(135·235·1345). He cross-multiplies to 126·1236·246·135·235·1345.
- Superscripts (3, 14, 2356, 1456, 23456) appear to be characteristic sums of the factors.
- He then tabulates triples of 4-fold products, e.g. {126 1236 246 2346 | 125 1235 245 2345 | 156 1356 456 3456} and {136 236 1346 2346 | 135 235 1345 2345 | 156 256 1456 2456}. These look like candidate term sets for three-term theta relations of Riemann-theta-formula type, sorted by characteristic sums.
- The final line '23456: 16 26 36 46 56 6' enumerates characteristics.
- No conclusion is drawn in this part.
errors: Line '(αγ−1)(αβ−1) − α²(βγ−1) = α² − α(β+γ) + βγ' is wrong as written. The correct right-hand side is α² − α(β+γ) + 1. Riemann repairs this on the next line by bringing in (1−α²)(βγ−1); the correct identity is (αγ−1)(αβ−1) − (α²−1)(βγ−1) = (α−β)(α−γ).
The third square root has denominator written (β−α)(α−β) (or (γ−α)(α−β)). For the stated value 236·1456/(456·1236) it must be (α−γ)(α−β); as written the radicand has the wrong sign or wrong factor.

Sign conventions are loose throughout. With unsigned symbols, (αγ−1)/((β−α)(β−γ)) comes out as −P25²/P45², not +P25²/P45². This is harmless if the symbols are antisymmetric or are squares of theta values.
The factorisations of αβ−1, α−β, etc. are asserted without derivation. They presuppose theta (Thomae/Rosenhain-type) identities not shown on this page.

deep.surprise_reason: This is consistent with Riemann's known (posthumously published) work on Abelian/theta functions with characteristic notation. The genus-2 theta-constant factorisations of Rosenhain moduli predate him (Göpel, Rosenhain) and Thomae systematised them by 1870. It is a notable working sheet but contains nothing beyond what is attributed to his school.

The three listed quantities sum to 1, giving a linear relation among the four quantities 1, ... (proportional to squares of P45,P15,P25,P35)
The factorisation α−β = P12P45/(P15P25) is the three-term (Plücker) relation P14P25−P24P15=P12P45 in the 2x2-minor model

(α−β)/(α−1/β) = β(α−β)/(αβ−1) equals the product written on the page

transcription_corrections: In α−γ the factor '4526' is correct as written; it denotes {2,4,5,6}, the complement of 13, consistent with the pairing pattern.
The item rendered as '1/((βγ−1)/((α−γ)(α−β)))' is a list entry: a '1' standing above the fraction (βγ−1)/((α−γ)(α−β)), not a reciprocal.
The third square root's denominator is probably meant as (γ−α)(α−β) or (α−γ)(α−β), not (β−α)(α−β).
The final unnumbered expression is the difference (αγ−1)(αβ−1)/((α−γ)(α−β)) − (α²−1)(βγ−1)/((α−γ)(α−β)) followed by '+1'. The intended content is that this difference equals 1.
Symbols like 1325, 425, 3425, 4536 are Riemann's unordered index sets (= 1235, 245, 2345, 3456).
The header lines (α p q r δ ε ζ ...) are too faint to read reliably; the transcription is uncertain there.
